text:
devon: heads up — eu-west-1 is showing a weird pattern: a ton of GPU pods Pending and a few GPUs sitting ~90% idle in a different AZ. pods are queueing instead of being scheduled across AZs. anyone else seeing this?

maria: yup saw it at 11:14. some pods fail with "0/8 nodes are available: node(s) didn't match Pod's nodeAffinity." Looks like a mix of zoneAffinity + topologySpread + gpu-family taints.

alex: can you paste the kubectl errors?

devon: here is one example from the deploy pipeline:

```
Events:
  Type     Reason            Age    From               Message
  ----     ------            ----   ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling  2m20s  default-scheduler  0/8 nodes are available: 3 node(s) didn't match node selector, 5 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate.
```

plus node list shows GPU nodes in eu-west-1a with taint gpu-group=alpha:NoSchedule and eu-west-1b has free GPUs but nodes labelled gpu-family=v100 while pods require gpu-family=a100.

liam: the a100 pool autoscaled down last night (we had a bug in the scale-down grace TTL) and some jobs were pinned to a100 by nodeAffinity. when new a100 nodes come up, they prefer to land in 1a due to our topology constraints. 1b remains with v100s.

maria: that explains the fragmentation — scheduling policy + autoscaler churn created a hole. but why aren't pods using v100 variants as fallback? we have model images that can run on v100 with quantized profile.

devon: current pod spec hard-requires "gpu-family: a100" in nodeAffinity. leftover from perf experiments. we changed it to strict to avoid noisy-neighbor perf regressions.

alex: can we relax affinity to prefer a100 but tolerate v100 as fallback? something like: preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution weight: 100 for a100, and tolerate v100 with a lower score?

liam: yes — also consider adding a toleration for the gpu-group taint on preemption-critical workloads, or a preemptible pool tag so lower-priority jobs can be evicted if capacity needed.

sre-bot: note: descheduler run at 03:00 removed some low-priority pods from 1b yesterday. autoscaler event: scaledDown 6 a100 nodes at 02:48.

ops-bot: metric spike: gpu-alloc-fragmentation_ratio in eu-west-1 at 11:12 = 0.68 (threshold 0.5)

maria: proposal: for immediate mitigation do two things — (1) update the pod templates for non-latency jobs to use preferredDuringScheduling for gpu-family, (2) bump scale-up lookahead for a100 pool to avoid aggressive scale-down at night.

devon: ack. i'll open a quick PR to change affinity on the batch job templates and set a rollout for canary. putting the a100 strict requirement back on latency-critical services only.

alex: also add a small descheduler job to consolidate idle GPUs once per hour? it helped before when we had fragmentation after spot preemptions.

liam: long-term we should expose a scheduling policy that maps job class -> acceptable gpu families + evict priority. then scheduler can pack cross-az or relax AZ affinity when cost/latency tradeoffs allow.

maria: agree. for now devon, can you list the affected deployment names so we can triage the highest-cost ones first?

devon: listing: infer-batch-ml, embed-indexer, nightly-quantize, hyperparam-search. i'll mark infer-batch-ml as high-priority to use fallback on v100.

alex: small FYI — billing shows wasted GPU-hours when fragmentation persists. finance pinged us this morning about a ~7% GPU cost surge month-over-month tied to eu-west-1.

maria: ok PR incoming in ~15m. after change we should monitor: Pending pods count, fragmentation_ratio, and tail latency for latency-critical routes.

liam: also let's add a temporary alert: if >50 Pending GPU pods for >5m in a region, run a remediation playbook that flips preferred->required on a canary subset and notifies infra-oncall.

devon: creating the PR and the playbook now. cc @maria @liam. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: deploy bot: PR #3421 created by devon -> infra/scheduler (WIP).

maria: thanks — will watch the canary and roll back if we see perf regressions.

alex: great catch — looks like a classic fragmentation + affinity mismatch. will follow up in eng-platform doc with proposed scheduler policy changes.
